text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English Lord Chancellor SIR THOMAS MOORE, who was executed by HENRY VIII for refusing to deny the authority of the Pope, was born in 1478.
English novelist CHARLES DICKENS, who wrote the much-loved "DAVID COPPERFIELD" and "OLIVER TWIST", was born on this day in 1812.
British keyboard player and songwriter STEVE BRONSKI was born in 1960. He was a key member of the band that was named after him. 'Bronski Beat' was formed in 1984.
American keyboard player with 'Bon Jovi' DAVID BRYAN (DAVID RASHBAUM) was born in 1962.
** EVENTS **
Austrian pschoanalyst ALFRED ADLER, the man who introduced the concept of the "inferiority complex", was born in 1870.
Artist RUSSELL DRYSDALE was born on this day in 1912.
UK bass player with a range of bands including 'Status Quo' ALAN LANCASTER was born in 1949. He moved to Australia after the group broke up and appeared sporadically with the 'Party Boys'.
British saxophonist and songwriter with 'UB40' BRIAN TRAVERS was born in 1959. He also directed most of their videos.
1845 : WILLIAM LLOYD calmly walked into the British
Museum and smashed the famous "Portland Vase" which had been dug-up in Rome 300 years earlier. The 2,000 pieces were expertly reassembled and the fractures weren't noticeable.
1863 : 185 people died as HMS ORPHEUS was wrecked on the
coast of New Zealand.
1886 : GEORGE WALKER discovered gold in Transvaal in
South Africa, while building a house.
1959 : Former Prime Minister of South Africa and the
architect of apartheid, DANIEL F. MALAN, died.
1960 : Israeli archaeologists unearthed a number of the
DEAD SEA scrolls.
1964 : 25-thousand fans packed New York's Kennedy Airport
as THE BEATLES arrived for their first American tour.
1971 : Swiss allowed women to vote.
1986 : LINDY CHAMBERLAIN was released from Darwin's

Berrimah jail after serving three years and three months for the murder of her baby daughter AZARIA. She was given an unconditional release by the Northern Territory government following the discovery of the baby's matinee jacket almost six years after the nine-week-old baby went missing. The CHAMBERLAINS always claimed a dingo had taken their baby from the tent at the Ayers Rock camp site. The discovery of the new evidence coincided with the release of a new report by the chief forensic scientist of South Australia DR ANDREW SCOTT, which

challenged the assessment of the forensic evidence used in convicting Mrs CHAMBERLAIN. In June 1987 MICHAEL and LINDY CHAMBERLAIN were both pardoned by the orthern Territory government and in September 1988 their convictions were quashed. The couple had maintained their innocence through two inquests, a seven-week trial, two higher court appeals and Justice MORLEY's 11-month Commission of Inquiry.
1988 : The Australian government dumped a proposal to
introduce pay-for-time local telephone calls.
1990 : American songwriter JIMMY VAN HEUSEN, who composed
the SINATRA hit "Come Fly With Me", died.
1990 : The Central Committee of the Soviet Communist
Party voted for a package of reforms, ending its monopoly on power.
1991 : The IRA fired motar bombs into Number 10 Downing
Street, the residence of British Prime Minister JOHN MAJOR.
